summary: This program builds a larger list of farmers' market products and then runs three separate stream pipelines over it: one that collects the distinct vendor names, one that formats a single vendor's products into a printable menu, and one that computes discounted prices for that vendor. Each pipeline lives in its own helper method so the transformations are easy to read.

lines.text: This is map in its simplest role: extracting one field from each object, so a stream of MarketProduct objects becomes a stream of vendor names.

Collecting into a Set discards duplicate vendor names automatically, which is why three Baker's Lane products yield one entry. A Set has no defined order, so the printed vendor list may not match the order the products were added.

Here map formats rather than extracts: it stitches two fields into a single display String, with the price rounded to two decimal places. The stream's element type changes from MarketProduct to String.
Computing the multiplier once, before the pipeline starts, keeps the lambda short and avoids repeating the subtraction for every product.
This map calculates a new value from the old one, producing a stream of Double prices; Math.max guards against a negative result if a discount fraction greater than 1 is ever passed in.
The pipeline only builds the list of formatted strings — printing is a separate step, which is what keeps the helper methods reusable and testable.
